title: End-to-End Autoregressive Image Generation with 1D Semantic Tokenizer
claim: Separately trained tokenizer and generator stages can be replaced by joint end-to-end training, which gives better scaling.
layout: 3 panels: stacked (a) and (b) on left, plot (c) at right
description: The figure has three panels. Panel (a), top left, shows conventional two-stage training. Stage 1 is an encoder, quantizer and decoder trained for reconstruction. Stage 2 is autoregressive prediction on the frozen tokens. Blue latent-token boxes and orange AR-prediction boxes are linked by black forward arrows and red gradient arrows, and small red-panda photos mark the inputs and reconstructions. Panel (b), bottom left, shows the end-to-end framework. A 1D encoder feeds an IBQ quantizer with a codebook. The quantizer feeds both the generative AR head and the reconstruction decoder. Red gradient arrows flow back from the generative loss to the tokenizer, and a legend explains the arrow types. Panel (c), right, is a line plot of FID against model size. Colored lines compare methods, and the red 'Ours' line is lowest and steepest.
caption: Overview of EOSTok that jointly trains an 1D vision tokenizer and an autoregressive generative model. (a) Conventional paradigms employ a two-stage training strategy. The tokenizer is trained on a reconstruction task. An autoregressive generative model is then trained on the token sequences encoded by the frozen tokenizer. (b) Our training framework jointly optimizes the tokenizer and the AR model, enabling end-to-end generative supervision to guide the tokenizer. (c) Our EOSTok model enjoys a superior scaling ability on the ImageNet 1K 256ˆ256 generation benchmark. We compare EOSTok to generative models with AR, mask, or diffusion modeling. Numbers are collected without guidance except for those with (*).
abstract: Autoregressive image modeling relies on visual tokenizers to compress images into compact latent representations. We design an end-to-end training pipeline that jointly optimizes reconstruction and generation, enabling direct supervision from generation results to the tokenizer. This contrasts with prior two-stage approaches that train tokenizers and generative models separately. We further investigate leveraging vision foundation models to improve 1D tokenizers for autoregressive modeling. Our autoregressive generative model achieves strong empirical results, including a state-of-the-art FID score of 1.48 without guidance on ImageNet 256x256 generation.
